newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Go-Video sees higher Q1 net.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Go-Video sees higher Q1 net.

text.p: Go-Video Inc, a maker of video electronic products, expects to post a sharp rise in fiscal first quarter profits, reflecting higher sales of its dual-deck video recorders.

In a telephone interview, Go-Video Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Roger Hackett said the company expects net income for the quarter, ended in June, to rise 70 percent, to more than $300,000, or about $0.03 a share, from $187,000, or $0.02 a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues are expected to top $9.5 million, versus $8.2 million a year ago.
The company is scheduled to report first quarter results next week.
Hackett said the improvement marks the fifth consecutive quarter the Scottsdale, Ariz.-based company has been profitable.

At the center Go-Video's company's improvement is a new, lower-priced dual tape deck that sells for $399 and has allowed the company to attract more customers at the retail level at the same time that it improves gross margins.

"We were able to introduce a new popularly-priced deck, which increased the size of our addressable market," Hackett said. "We've in excess of a 40 percent unit increase since we introduced the new product at the new price point."

Currently, the vast majority of the company's tape decks are sold in the United States, but with overseas sales accounting for two-thirds of all VCR sales, Hackett said the company is looking to ship more machines abroad.
Last month the company started to sell its dual-deck VCR in Japan; it hopes to expand into Europe by the fall.
For the fiscal year ending in March 1998, the company expects revenues to grow 15 to 20 percent and earnings to grow even faster.
Go-Video derives most of its revenues from the dual deck VCR product line, but it also is developing home theater systems and video security products for the commerical and consumer market.
Hackett said he expects the security division to provide a material contribution to the company as early as this year. The home theater unit is still in the development stage.
Hackett said the company also expects to have a digital video disc product in the next 12 months in case demand for higher quality DVD machines takes off.
He said the company also plans to continue to spend on advertising in the peak holiday selling season this fall, with marketing expenses budgeted at around 3 to 4 percent of revenues.
